thread:
alex: Heads-up, SFO popped P99 latency around 10:12 UTC, looks correlated with a sudden bump in RTT to a handful of ISP peers. Seeing kernel selector fallbacks in the logs too. anyone already digging?

maya: I started a quick check — KV cache hit-rate dropped from ~87% -> 32% at the same time window. Could be cross-pop routing sending cold prefixes back to SFO.

sam: Net metrics show a spike in retransmits on sfo-pop-b8 egress to AS16509 (big cloud provider) from 10:11:30 -> 10:14:20. TTL and latency jitter look nasty.

netbot: Incident detected: sfo-pop-b8 - network_peer_jitter - elevated_rtt(>200ms) - window 10:11:15 to 10:15:00 UTC. Notifying #eng-network.

jon: If packets re-order / retransmit we'll see more kernel fallback because the kernel-selector times out waiting for optimized GEMM happy-path. I have logs showing: 
```
[10:12:02] KernelSelector: selected optimized_conv_v2 for model-id:rw-7b
[10:12:12] KernelSelector: timeout waiting for vectorized-kernel -> fallback to generic_gemm
[10:12:13] KVCache: miss_eviction=42 miss_repopulate=37
```

maya: also saw batching heuristics shrink batch sizes automatically around 10:12 (we reduce max-batch to keep latency under SLO). That's why throughput dropped.

priya: Can we confirm whether this was noisy neighbor on local host (GPU saturation) vs network-induced latency? Any perf profiles?

profiling-bot: Attached flame sample (collected 10:12:20) - top frames: scheduler_wait, recv_tcp, kernel_selector_timeout, generic_gemm_exec.

alex: Good — profiling-bot confirms scheduler_wait is dominated by network recv latency. Suggest we isolate by pinning flows to alternate path/POP to see if latency drops.

dylan: I pushed a temporary routing rule to prefer sfo-peer-3 for traffic to AS16509 at 10:18 UTC, can folks watch p99/kv-hit and kernel logs for next 10m?

sam: After the reroute: p50 stable, p99 dropped from 450ms -> 125ms over next 3mins, KVCache hit-rate climbed back to ~78% by 10:22. KernelSelector logs show fewer fallbacks.

jon: TL;DR: root cause = transient ISP peering jitter -> increased recv latency -> scheduler reduces batch size and KernelSelector timeouts -> fallbacks to generic kernels -> throughput drop + higher p99 + KV cache repop churn.

maya: Action items: 1) add BGP/peering alert threshold to catch jitter sooner; 2) make KernelSelector timeout adaptive to upstream jitter (longer when recv latency high); 3) add a conservative KV rewarming backoff to avoid thrash.

priya: + add synthetic probes to the SFO->AS16509 path to detect jitter before it impacts production. I'll open a ticket and ping infra.

alex: thanks all. I'll open an incident doc and assign follow-ups. tagging @oncall for the rest. :thumbsup:

netbot: Incident update posted: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-sfo-peer-jitter (auto-created).

10:12:11.125 IP 52.94.XX.XX > 10.2.0.8: Flags [P.], seq 1:1401, ack 1, win 41200, options [nop,nop,TS val 987654999 ecr 123456789], length 1400
10:12:11.130 IP 52.94.XX.XX > 10.2.0.8: Flags [R], seq 1402, win 0, length 0

jon: We'll prototype making kernel-selector resilient to jitter by: (a) tracking recent recv RTT histogram per egress peer, (b) scaling timeout = base * (1 + p95_rtt/50ms). I'll put a PR up.

alex: perfect. closing thread here — please post PR/incident links back to the ticket when ready.
